To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the shelf-break of the Great Barrier reef is a hotspot of biodiversity and abundance of fishes and 2) that depth is a strong determinant of the composition and structure of fish assemblages.

(1) Fish assemblages are distinct with depth in the GBR shelf break; (2) Fish species richness decreases rapidly between 100–260 m depth; (3) Commercially valuable species are absent from shallow depths, and (4) The shelf break of the GBR is home to high levels of biodiversity.
